result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers spot the label-versus-specific pattern and cite the right examples, and both note the small sample size. A has more varied options and a stronger split-test plan, but its copy invents content the issue may not deliver: snow-free trails, a pole mistake that's 'wrecking your knees', 'three quick fixes' and a question 'we get every summer'. B sticks strictly to the three named items and adds a useful caution about Apple's privacy features inflating opens. However, B's options are less varied and its test plan of changing one thing per send is weaker than a true split test. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers find the same pattern: label-style subjects got 15-19% and specific ones got 34-38%. B's table makes it especially clear. B's options make up content and promises the issue may not keep, such as the pole mistake 'wrecking your knees', 'snow-free', 'a question we get every summer' and 'three quick fixes'. Several of them also lean on bait. B also overstates that deliverability is fine, while A stays within the named contents and is more careful about what six sends can show.
